say.text: Jumada II, 564 AH: March, 1169. Shirkuh has been vizier of Egypt for two months and five days.
A new illness came upon him, an inflammation of the throat, and it was of this that he died.
It is a poor sort of end for a man who thought he would die on a field.
Rest your throat, uncle. Do not speak.
You have said that to me many times, and I have not once listened. Hear me this time.
They will tell you that you are too young, and too gentle, and that you have no troops. Remember who counted the bread in Alexandria.
Shirkuh died on Sunday the 22nd of Jumada II, 564 AH: 23 March, 1169. The day and the cause are told differently in different books. Some said a poisoned robe; the Codex gives the rumour as a rumour.
He said that I would manage.
His body was buried in the palace of the vizierate, and was later taken to Medina.
